events.subtitle: Baltimore Recital Debut — Gregor Piatigorsky Memorial Concert
events.factual_description: Shriver Hall Concert Series presents Pablo Ferrández in his Baltimore recital debut on Sunday, October 11, 2026 at 5:30 PM at Shriver Hall on the Johns Hopkins University Homewood Campus. A 4:30 PM pre-concert talk with Peabody Institute scholar Anna Celenza precedes the approximately two-hour concert. The announced solo-cello program is J.S. Bach's Cello Suite No. 3 in C major, BWV 1009; Gaspar Cassadó's Cello Suite; J.S. Bach's Cello Suite No. 1 in G major, BWV 1007; and Benjamin Britten's Cello Suite No. 1, Op. 72. The recital opens Shriver Hall Concert Series' 61st season and is designated the Gregor Piatigorsky Memorial Concert. Ferrández's official artist calendar independently confirms an October 11 Shriver Hall solo recital in Baltimore featuring works by Bach, Cassadó and Britten; it also lists the same repertoire family for a Toronto solo recital on October 8, supporting the non-scarcity priority judgment.

en.why_it_matters: One cello carries the whole argument: two Bach suites framing Cassadó's Spanish, dance-charged suite and Britten's first Rostropovich-inspired suite. Ferrández's Baltimore debut puts technique, tone and the instrument's ability to imply an entire harmonic world under a spotlight, while the Piatigorsky Memorial context gives the recital a lineage specific to the cello rather than generic classical prestige.
en.trip_verdict: If a Baltimore afternoon is already plausible, this is a strong reason to choose October 11 and make the short trip north. I would not restructure a corridor itinerary around this date alone; the solo program is also being performed in Toronto three days earlier and belongs to an active recital season.

es.why_it_matters: Un solo violonchelo carga con todo el argumento: dos suites de Bach enmarcan la suite española y cargada de danza de Cassadó y la primera suite de Britten escrita para Rostropóvich. El debut de Ferrández en Baltimore pone bajo la lupa la técnica, el sonido y la capacidad del instrumento para insinuar un mundo armónico entero; el contexto del Memorial Piatigorsky le da además una genealogía específicamente chelista, no sólo prestigio clásico genérico.
es.trip_verdict: Si una tarde en Baltimore ya es viable, ésta es una buena razón para escoger el 11 de octubre y hacer el viaje corto hacia el norte. No reorganizaría un itinerario del corredor únicamente por esta fecha: el mismo programa de recital aparece en Toronto tres días antes y forma parte de una temporada activa.
